properties.statement:
`propose_heal`'s RECEIPT MISDESCRIBES ITS OWN SCOPE AT BOTH ENDS: it names a target the caller never chose, and its zero cannot say whether the scorer ran. Reported as two findings by sb-boss (`79d03ab3`) 2026-08-15 on the shared StoryFlow graph; BOTH REPRODUCED HERE on reflow2's own design, and one of them is invisible to the self-host for a structural reason worth naming.

① A `target_id` NOBODY ASKED FOR. The tool takes only `strategy` and `max_operations` — there is NO target parameter — yet the reply carries `target_id`. Their measurement: 4 Projects in the graph, `target_id: proj:dndwright` (alphabetically first), while `issues_addressed` spanned the WHOLE graph including a sibling library and a 121-node cluster. The sweep was global and the label was local. REPRODUCED HERE: `propose_heal{strategy: balanced, max_operations: 10}` returned `target_id: "proj:reflow2"`.

⚠️ AND THIS IS WHY WE COULD NOT HAVE FOUND IT: reflow2's graph holds EXACTLY ONE Project, so the label is accidentally correct here and the defect is unobservable. It needs a multi-Project design to show, which is what a fleet sharing one graph across three bosses has and the maintainer does not. Self-host blindness, and the same shape as F23.

② THE ZERO IS VACUOUS AND NOTHING SAYS SO — the sharper half, because this fleet runs it as a SAFETY GATE. They hold a standing stop on `apply_heal` whose lift condition is 'propose_heal pairs NONE of the five control pairs', and ran it as the read-only evidence step: `operations: []`, `would_destroy: []`, `skipped_operations: []`, 0 of 7 control pairs paired. It reads exactly like a PASS. It is not: no duplicate-class defect existed, so the pair scorer NEVER RAN, and 'it paired none of the seven' is trivially true of nothing. A prior run on 0.24.0 produced 10 structural Merge operations, every one deleting a node — so the shape changed completely and nothing in the output says whether the scorer improved or simply had no input.

REPRODUCED HERE, same shape: `propose_heal` → `operations: []`, summary '9 issue(s) addressed: 0 structural op(s), 9 awaiting generation, 0 skipped'. `detect_defects` → 16 defects, of which contradiction 4, disconnected_community 5, orphan_node 4, unresolved_setup 3, and DUPLICATE-CLASS ZERO. So our own 0 is vacuous by the identical mechanism, and only a second tool call distinguishes it from a real pass.

⭐ THEIR THIRD IDEA IS THE GENERAL ONE AND IS WORTH MORE THAN EITHER FIX: when a detector contributes zero findings, say whether it was EXERCISED AND FOUND NOTHING or HAD NOTHING TO EXAMINE. That is the difference between a check that passed and a check that could not fail. reflow2 already does this elsewhere — `chg:a-null-and-a-vacuous-zero-now-say-which-they-are` gave scoped `detect_gaps` exactly that treatment, and dragon Boss named it a WIN in the same log. So the pattern is accepted doctrine here and `propose_heal` has not received it.

CHEAPEST FIXES, theirs: (1) report the input set — `merge_candidates_considered: 0` beside `operations: []`; (2) distinguish `no_candidates` from `no_operations_proposed` in the summary string, which today render identically; (3) say `scope: "whole design"` when no target was given rather than naming a Project the caller did not pick, or accept an optional scope argument as `detect_gaps` and `detect_defects` both already do.

NOT ESTABLISHED: whether `apply_heal` carries the same label, and whether any other tool emits a `target_id` it was not given.
